ЧЕРНОВИКИ

DRAFT 1 (digest)
SHAPE: digest
BODY: A few recent data releases and market updates that caught my eye:

- Demographic shift in Polish housing. In 2025, Poland recorded 406,000 deaths against only 134,000 new developer apartments. As generational wealth transfers pick up, 80,000 to 120,000 inherited apartments could hit the market annually, challenging developer pricing power.

- Bank Millennium cut its standard savings account rate to 0.50% starting August 1, 2026. This shows how banks protect their net interest margins by aggressively lowering rates on sticky retail deposits before the central bank even cuts official rates.

- Polish gas imports rose 23% in 2025 to 213.5 TWh, with LNG making up 42.9% of that volume. This shift highlights the growing cost of energy security as expensive maritime LNG replaces cheaper pipeline gas.

DRAFT 3 (C)
SHAPE: C
BODY: Many buyers and developers believe that Poland faces a permanent housing shortage that will keep property prices climbing forever. The supply of new builds cannot keep up with demand, so prices must rise.

But a massive demographic supply shock is coming from outside the developer market.

In 2025, Poland recorded 406,000 deaths. In contrast, developers completed only 134,000 new apartments. I compared these figures from the RynekPierwotny report, and the difference is striking. Even if only 20% to 30% of those estates are eventually sold or rented out by heirs, that still brings 80,000 to 120,000 apartments to the market every year.

This secondary supply, mostly older panel-block apartments, is nearly equal to what developers build annually. The structural shortage narrative ignores this massive, non-developer pipeline that will inevitably dilute pricing power in secondary cities.
FIGURES:
- 2025 -> Story [2] source text
- 406,000 -> Story [2] source text ("406 tys.")
- 134,000 -> Story [2] source text ("134 tys.")
- 20% to 30% -> Story [2] source text ("20-30 proc.")
- 80,000 to 120,000 -> Story [2] source text ("80-120 tys.")
SOURCE: https://www.bankier.pl/wiadomosc/Wielka-plyta-zagrozi-deweloperom-Tysiace-odziedziczonych-mieszkan-trafia-na-sprzedaz-9176697.html
WHY_THIS_ONE: Challenges the dominant real estate narrative using a logical, data-backed supply-side argument that does not require deep real estate expertise to defend.
VERDICT: POST
WHY: The comparison between deaths and completions is simple, mathematically sound, and directly addresses a major macroeconomic theme in Poland.
